To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) page loadable columns are a new data structure for in-memory columnar data, that (2) can be used for cold data in a columnar database, and that (3) have a small overhead in terms of resource consumption and performance, while providing the benefits of partial loading.

(i) page loadable columns can significantly reduce the mandatory memory consumption of a table by 30% to 40% while incurring an average performance penalty of 5% and a worst case performance penalty of 10%; and (ii) page loadable tables can extend the in-memory lifetime by a factor of two.
page loadable columns can significantly reduce the memory footprint of in-memory column stores and can extend the in-memory lifetime for partially loaded columns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new in-memory data structure that is able to load and evict columns on demand.
the question: How can we make the best use of the limited memory in an in-memory system?
the design of in-memory algorithms that operate on a partially loaded columnar data structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
page loadable columns are an interesting approach for cold data, but they are too expensive in terms of performance overhead for hot data.
page loadable columns are an interesting alternative to regular in-memory columns for cold data.
page loadable columns can be used to extend the in-memory column lifetime and reduce the mandatory memory footprint of a column, at a small performance overhead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
page loadable columnar access can be a valuable alternative to regular columnar access when there are memory constraints, and the performance overhead is acceptable for the application.
page loadable columns are a promising alternative approach to deal with memory pressure in in-memory columnar systems.

we propose an alternative approach to the traditional in-memory columnar design, which we call page loadable column, to reduce the mandatory memory footprint per column, and to extend the in-memory lifetime for columns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the page loadable column approach can be used to improve the performance of in-memory databases when the data working set does not fit into the main memory.
the performance overhead of page loadable column is small and can be compensated by a reduction of the mandatory memory footprint of the column.
page loadable columns are an effective alternative to the regular columns for applications with a large memory footprint.
